neighbours.label: routes of contamination or infection: how a pathogen or toxin gets in (through contaminated food and water, sources include)
fire: Hepatitis A is usually caught through contaminated food and water.
Children can absorb lead through peeling paint and household dust.
Salmonella often spreads through raw eggs and undercooked chicken.
The parasite enters the body through unwashed vegetables and fruit.
Mercury reaches people mainly through eating contaminated fish.
The virus is passed on through shared needles and blood.
Asbestos fibres get into the lungs through dust from old insulation.
Typhoid is spread through sewage in drinking water.
quiet: Hepatitis A was first identified by researchers in the 1970s.
Children can learn about lead by visiting the science museum.
Salmonella was named after an American veterinary scientist.
The parasite has a complex life cycle with several stages.
Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
The virus was isolated in a laboratory in Uganda.
Asbestos was once praised as a miracle building material.
Typhoid Mary worked as a cook in New York.
